minutes.headline: Assessors heard lakefront residents appeal good/average land ratings from the MFS review, then moved to executive session.
minutes.summary: The board explained the first batch of MFS abatement reviews and how good, average and low-average waterfront ratings change 2023 land values. Most of the meeting was remote public comment from lake residents asking for average or lower ratings. The board then moved into executive session; the vote is only partly audible.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors moved into executive session at the end of the meeting; the vote count is only partly audible in the captions.
Most of the meeting was public comment from lakefront residents asking for average or lower waterfront ratings than the good rating assigned in the MFS abatement review.
The chair explained how good, average and low-average ratings translate into abatement shares of the difference between the 2022 and 2023 land values.
The board said notice letters with new assessments would go out after the reviews finish, within about two weeks at most.
The next meeting was set for Thursday, May 25, to wrap up the first batch of reviews.

why_it_matters: A waterfront rating of good, average or low-average changes the 2023 land value on which a lakefront owner's tax bill is based, so residents on the lake may see different assessments depending on how their lot is rated.
Residents learn their rating only when the notice letter arrives, and several speakers said they had not been told it, so the letter is the point at which they can check it.
